lessons_control.note: pre_lessons is each hunter's own sum before it read researcher_us/LESSONS.md. edge_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, which is the only thing that can tell the guidance file apart from a habit.

language_control.note: RETIRED 2026-09-22: the European and Canadian hunters now run one bilingual pass and emit no freeze, so this is 0/0 on every run sealed after that date. On earlier runs pre_local is each hunter's own sum after the ENGLISH pass and before the local pass; eu_resolve.py ranks it against the same realised move as the key, per market, and does not pool the UK (where the second pass varied source locality) with Germany and France (where it varied language).

note: Ranked on impact_sum: the hunters' signed per-finding sizes, added up, in points of spot. No call and no threshold -- cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what keeps the ranking question answerable at every k. `conviction` (abs of the key) is where the direction skill lives: over all events the sign is a coin flip, above the median conviction it is 74%. conviction_floor is a floor on emphasis in the note, never a filter on this file. Everything under `diagnostics` was measured as neutral or subtractive and decides nothing -- see researcher_us/EDGE_ANALYSIS.md.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-17, with Q3 already closed and 13 days before the print, BOS restated that full-year 2026 revenue AND net income will 'exceed 2025 levels' (>$50.6m and >$3.6m). H1 net income was $2.1m, so H2 must be above $1.5m. The Q3 consensus of $0.06 EPS (about $0.42m on 7.06m shares) would leave Q4 needing about $1.1m+, above any quarter except Q2 2026's $1.4m. Q4 has only $11m of scheduled backlog deliveries. Reaffirming net income with Q3 already known therefore points to Q3 net income nearer $0.6-0.8m, about $0.08-0.11 EPS, against the $0.06 bar. Operating leverage is high: opex is about $2.3m a quarter and gross margin 23-24%, so each $1m of revenue above $11.5m adds about $0.03 of EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS against consensus has moved this name in both directions. Q2 2026 (2026-08-20): $0.19 vs $0.13 consensus, +3.5% (4.53 to 4.69). Q1 2026 (2026-05-28): $0.11 vs $0.14 with revenue down y/y, -9.7%. Q3 2025 (2025-11-25): beat plus guide raise, +10.1%. Q1 2025 (2025-05-29): record $15m revenue, +19.8%. Q4 2025 (2026-03-31): 2026 guide flat on 2025, -10.2%. Closes from the Yahoo chart v8 daily bars.

findings.finding: The Q3-end backlog is a record $35m, up from $31m at Q2 end and $24m at year-end 2025. Its timing has shifted: about $24m is scheduled for 2027 and only about $11m for Q4 2026, against about $11m beyond 2026 and $20m due in H2 2026 at Q2 end. That is roughly $13m of new 2027-dated orders in one quarter, so 2027 starts with deliveries equal to about 47% of 2026's guided revenue already contracted. It also means the Q4 revenue that closes the >$51m guide must partly come from orders booked and shipped within the quarter. The video call will likely be asked about 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog headlines have not reliably moved the stock. Backlog was flat at $31m in Q2 2026 and the stock still rose +3.5% on the EPS beat. The Q1 2026 backlog jump to $31m (+29%) came with a -9.7% day because revenue fell. This release itself bought +2.65% on 2026-11-17.

findings.finding: The shekel weakened about 2.9% against the US dollar in Q3 2026, after strengthening about 5.9% in Q2 (Bank of Israel Q3 FX market report). The CFO had put the H1 2026 opex hit from dollar weakness at about $0.6m, so Q3 should carry less of that drag than Q2's exit rate. This is a small tailwind for Q3 net income relative to the run rate the consensus was built on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No isolated reaction to FX. FX was cited as the reason the net-income guide was held, not raised, at Q1 2026 (-9.7% day).

findings.finding: The 2026-11-17 release, written with Q3 known, kept the full-year guide at 'exceed 2025 levels' rather than raising it. So the print most likely carries a reaffirmation, not the kind of raise that bought +10.1% on 2025-11-25. On this name a flat guide was sold (-10.2% on 2026-03-31).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide raise on 2025-11-25: +10.1%. Guide flat on 2025 levels on 2026-03-31: -10.2%. Revenue guide raised to 'exceed $51m' but net income held on 2026-05-28: -9.7%. Net-income guide raised on 2026-08-20: +3.5%.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None sourced for NAT on insurance or other one-off comparisons.

findings.finding: The second of two 2003-built Suezmaxes sold in Q1 (a US$25m net sale, vessel debt-free) was delivered early in Q3 after being trapped in Hormuz. Q3 should therefore book a vessel-sale gain, which could lift headline EPS above the $0.18 consensus and well above Benzinga's $0.10.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 carried a vessel-sale gain as well; no price reaction to it was sourced.

findings.finding: The Q4 2026 forward read in the report will be strong. NAT's Nov 9 letter said its last 10 spot fixtures (about 60 days each, mostly Q4) average about $144,000/day TCE (range $59k-$347k), with about 50% of the fleet spot and opex under $10k/day. findings.finding: Suezmax spot collapsed in November. TD20 WAF-UKC went from $18.27/bbl to $11.01/bbl in the week to Nov 6 and to $7.86/bbl by Nov 13, and several Suezmax and Aframax routes lost 50%+ of their earnings, on Hormuz diplomacy and the Russia-Ukraine talks. NAT's remaining open Q4 days (about 50% of the fleet is spot) and its outlook wording therefore face a weaker market than the $144k fixtures. Kpler expected a partial recovery.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock is -20.5% over 20 sessions into the print (baseline), which is the market's response to this series already.

outside_window.finding: Suezmax orderbook approaching 30% of the existing fleet (Okeanis management) and NAT's two 2028 newbuildings at $86m each: medium-term supply and capex, irrelevant to the one-session window.

So the stock enters a bmo print with a speculative premium on a stock that was 0.93 four sessions ago.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: May 2026, the closest analog: 1.16 to 1.50 (+29%) on May 22 into the May 26 Q1 release, 1.57 on May 26, then 1.25 on May 27 (-20.4%) and 1.14 on May 28 (Yahoo chart bars). The run built before the print and unwound within two sessions.

Q1 2026 (May 26): +4.7% on the day after a +29% pre-print spike, then -20.4% on May 27. Q2 2026 (Sep 1, bmo): 1.39 to 1.24, -10.8%. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This finding is the reaction history: three of three prints in 2026 closed lower within two sessions. The Q2 revenue beat with an EPS miss against a disputed $0.10 bar was sold -10.8%.

findings.finding: Q3 EPS should come in at or above the $0.04 bar, and revenue should clear the stale $21.5-22.5M consensus. Q2 revenue was $29.0M: trade revenues $5.80M plus voyage/time-charter $23.20M. Q3 adds Q-Shipping management fees (nine managed vessels from Jul 1, three more taken over in Q3) on a ~60-vessel commercially managed fleet. Q2 G&A of $5.57M included $1.8M of cash bonuses, against Q1 G&A of about $3.56M. If Q3 G&A normalises, operating income gains about $1.5M on a Q2 base of $1.82M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 revenue beat (29.0 vs ~21.4-24.4M) came with an EPS miss against a disputed bar and was sold -10.8%. This name has not paid for revenue beats.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after Heidmar last spoke show Q4 2026 mid-size tanker bookings at extremes: Teekay Tankers has 58% of Q4 Suezmax spot days at $272,000/day and Aframax/LR2 at $208,300, against Q3 averages of $106,437 and $67,552; DHT has 50% of Q4 VLCC spot days at $509,100. Heidmar runs Suezmax/Aframax pools and earns commissions on pool gross, and in September it guided that 'rates to remain elevated and potentially strengthen further' in Q4/Q1. The Nov 30 call is the first time it can quantify Q4 pool earnings.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 (Sep 1) carried similar bullish rate commentary ('Suezmaxes in the Mediterranean / Black Sea are at historical highs') and the stock fell -10.8%. Forward commentary has not been paid for at this name.

findings.finding: Q3 realised mid-size spot rates fell slightly from Q2 at the closest listed peer: Teekay Suezmax $106,437 vs $109,171 (-2.5%), Aframax/LR2 $67,552 vs $74,149 (-8.9%). Heidmar's Q3 pool commissions and relet margins (Q2: voyage/TC revenue $23.2M against charter-in and other $21.4M) therefore have no rate tailwind quarter on quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No HMR-specific history of reacting to rate-driven misses. Prior prints were sold regardless of the rate backdrop.

findings.finding: Heidmar has a $20M committed equity purchase facility with B. Riley Principal Capital II, under which up to 11,080,332 shares are registered for resale. The POS AM went effective June 10, 2026, and the facility runs 36 months. The company can sell shares at its discretion into a spike, and BRPC II resells them. Against a 6.04M float this is a supply overhang on a +57% run. The company has no visible need for the money: $28.7M cash, positive operating cash flow of $7.7M in H1, an asset-light model, and no acquisition named.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no disclosed draw. Weighted basic shares rose only from 58.24M (Q2'25) to 59.59M (Q2'26), so usage looks minimal so far.

findings.finding: The CEO (Pankaj Khanna, also a 10% owner via Rhea Marine at 26.24M shares) filed Form 4s, late, for small purchases: 20,000 shares at $1.22 (Jun 24) and 15,000 at $1.30 (Sep 1, the Q2 print day), about $44k in total. Form 144 proposed sales were filed by other holders on Jun 11, Jun 26 and Jul 6.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell -10.8% on the day the CEO bought.

findings.finding: Director Andreas Konialidis stepped down on Oct 13, 2026, with 'no disagreement'. The company said it would search for a replacement 'in due course'. This is the only company release between the Q2 print and the Q3 date notice.
